title: ENS resolution, Ransomwhere payment addresses, TON explorer and the transaction-graph policy (batch p3-G09-1)
owner: batch p3-G09-1 (P209 ens_resolver, P210 ransomwhere, P213 crypto_tx_graph, P214 ton_explorer)

attributes.ens_primary_name: ENS primary name (reverse record) set by the owner of the resolved Ethereum address, as reported by ENSData
attributes.ens_reverse_verified: bool: the ENS name and the primary name of the address it resolves to agree (forward and reverse records match)
attributes.ens_reverse_record: reverse-record status of an Ethereum address on ENS, e.g. 'no ENS primary name set (says nothing about the wallet)'
attributes.ens_text_records: ENS text records as set by the name owner (self-asserted, unverified): {record key: cleaned text <= 300 chars}
attributes.ens_wallets: multichain address records of an ENS name set by its owner: {chain: address} (self-asserted except the resolved ETH address)
attributes.ens_profile: descriptive ENS records of a name (description, avatar, header, pgp, contentHash, resolverAddress...), cleaned and capped at 300 chars
attributes.ens_rejected_records: ENS text records that were not usable identifiers (javascript: URLs, invalid handles, non-strings): list of {record, reason}
attributes.ransomwhere_status: result of the offline Ransomwhere match, e.g. 'not in the Ransomwhere dataset (dataset last updated 2024-10-29); a miss means nothing'
attributes.ransomware_payments: historical ransomware payments to an address per Ransomwhere: {family, tx_count, total_btc, total_usd, first_payment, last_payment, balance_btc, transactions [<= 5 {hash, time, btc, usd}]}
attributes.ton_address_forms: forms of a TON address: {raw ('wc:HEX'), bounceable (EQ...), non_bounceable (UQ...), workchain, testnet}
attributes.ton_wallet: TON wallet state from Toncenter walletInformation: {balance_ton, wallet_type, seqno, status, last_transaction_lt}
attributes.ton_collectible: Telegram collectible (Fragment NFT) behind a +888 number or a collectible username: {kind, token, nft_item, collection, on_sale, sale_contract, owner, transfer_date, transfer_date_note}

tags.crowdsourced: the data comes from a crowdsourced dataset (user submissions, partial and skewed coverage)
tags.collectible_owner: current owner wallet of a Telegram collectible (+888 number or username NFT): a dated lead, ownership can change, never identity proof

relations.ens_text_record: ENS name or wallet -> identifier its owner wrote into an ENS text record (twitter, github, url, email...): self-asserted, unverified
relations.ens_address_record: ENS name -> address of another chain its owner set as an ENS address record (self-asserted)
relations.current_nft_owner: Telegram collectible (+888 number or collectible username) -> TON wallet that currently owns its NFT (ownership can change; a lead, never identity proof)
